{{Quote|Remember that some of the greatest Mandalores were born or grew up far from our homeworld. Mandalore the Binder was born the son of a rug weaver on Harswee.|The writer of ''Ba'jurne Kyr'tsad Mando'ad''|<ref name="TBHC" />}}
'''Mandalore the Binder''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] the son of a [[Unidentified rug weaver|rug weaver]] on [[Harswee]],<ref name="TBHC" /> a celestial body known for its luxurious loom-woven [[Carpet/Legends|carpet]] exports.<ref name="TCWIV">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Incredible Vehicles]]''</ref> At some point between approximately [[7000 BBY]] and [[60 BBY/Legends|60 BBY]],<ref name="Date">Per ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]'', Mandalore the Binder ruled as [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|Mandalore]] after [[Mandalore the First/Legends|Mandalore the First]], whose reign ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' dates to approximately [[7000 BBY]]. ''The Bounty Hunter Code'' also establishes that ''[[Ba'jurne Kyr'tsad Mando'ad]]'', which mentions Mandalore the Binder's past reign, was supposedly [[Author/Legends|authored]] by [[Tor Vizsla]]&mdash;an authorship the authenticity of which was doubted by [[Jango Fett]]&mdash;at some point after the [[Battle of Galidraan]], which occurred in [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]] per ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''. Fett [[Showdown on Corellia|killed]] Vizsla during the main flashbacks of [[Jango Fett: Open Seasons 4|''Jango Fett: Open Seasons'' 4]], the events of which ''[[The Cestus Deception]]'' and ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' date to approximately three [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after the Battle of Galidraan, or around [[41 BBY/Legends|41 BBY]]. In addition, according to [[Jango Fett: Open Seasons 2|''Jango Fett: Open Seasons'' 2]], Fett also held the title of Mandalore from the time of the [[Battle of Korda Six|death]] of the previous Mandalore, [[Jaster Mereel]], up until&mdash;per ''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''&mdash;his own [[Death/Legends|death]], which took place in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] per ''The New Essential Chronology''. Per ''The Essential Guide to Warfare'', Mereel became Mandalore in [[60 BBY/Legends|60 BBY]], and ''Open Seasons'' 2 dates his death to thirty years before the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]] and thereby around [[52 BBY/Legends|52 BBY]] per ''The New Essential Chronology''. Therefore, Mandalore the Binder must have ruled as Mandalore at some point between approximately 7000 [['ABY-BBY' dating system/Legends|BBY]] and 60 BBY.</ref> they rose to claim the title of [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']],<ref name="TBHC" /> the traditional ruler of the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] clans.<ref name="TMPaC">{{InsiderCite|86|The Mandalorians: People and Culture}}</ref> Some time after Mandalore the Binder's reign, they were remembered in ''[[Ba'jurne Kyr'tsad Mando'ad]]'', a manifesto of the [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]] splinter group. The manifesto was claimed to have been [[Author/Legends|written]] by the group's founder, [[Tor Vizsla]]&mdash;although Death Watch's opponent [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] questioned that authorship. Jango's [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] son [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] later included the manifesto in the [[Book/Legends|book]] ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code]]''<ref name="TBHC" /> at some point between [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] and [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].<ref name="TBHCCreation">Per ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]'', ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code]]'' was created after the [[Death/Legends|death]] of [[Greedo/Legends|Greedo]] but before the [[Great ReSynchronization calendar|date]] 39:3:22, which corresponds to [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] per the reasoning [[Template:YearMathGRS|here]]. {{Film|IV}} depicts Greedo's death during events ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates to [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]].</ref>

Mandalore the Binder wore a suit of [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|Mandalorian armor]] consisting of a [[Helmet/Legends|helmet]] and body [[Armor/Legends|armor]] over their torso, [[Limb/Legends|arms]], and legs. Their right [[Gauntlet/Legends|gauntlet]] featured two spikes, and they wore a [[Kama/Legends|''kama'']] around their waist.<ref name="TBHC" />

==Behind the scenes==
Mandalore the Binder was mentioned in the [[2013]] reference book ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''.<ref name="TBHC" />
